To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the S5 semantics is: (1) a sound and complete model of the strict mode of JavaScript, (2) a model of the semantics of getters and setters that matches their intended behavior, (3) a model of eval that matches its intended behavior and that can be extended to handle the semantics of with, (4) a model of with that matches its intended semantics, and (5) an accurate model of the semantics for the JavaScript language.

(a) accessors are best modeled as a combination of a function and an expression, (b) eval is a function with a special argument, (c) the eval function is best modeled as a function that returns a function, and (d) accessors are not needed to implement eval, and eval is not needed to implement accessors
• S5 is a sound and complete specification of the strict mode of ECMAScript 2011 (JavaScript) that has been tested against a conformance suite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can a formal semantics be developed for the core language that is small enough to be tested and that captures the behavior of the language?
the following questions. How should accessors be defined? What is the meaning of eval? What is the relationship between accessors and eval?
the following questions: What is the precise semantics for accessors and eval in the ECMAScript language? How can the semantics be tested against the real world?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
accessors and eval are not well specified in JavaScript, and that this is a problem.
S5 is correct and complete with respect to the JavaScript standard.
the semantics of accessors and eval in S5 is sound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S5 is a practical and useful formal semantics for a real-world language.
S5 has been used to develop a new JavaScript conformance suite that includes accessors and eval, and that S5 is a useful tool for understanding these features and for testing implementations.
S5 provides a tested semantics for getters and setters, and a semantics for eval that is consistent with the rest of S5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to write an executable specification for JavaScript.
a formal specification of a large, complex, and widely-used language can be tested against real-world test suites.
the semantics for accessors and eval can be made simple and intuitive, and that the resulting semantics is testable and can serve as a useful basis for further study.
